Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 96, verses 1–5:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called al-‘Alaq (the Clot), because the word "al-‘alaq" (a moist clot of blood) occurs at its beginning.

Some of the Surah's Aims

• To show the wondrous power of God in creating man and teaching him what he did not know, and to speak of man's arrogance and rebellion against God's commands because of the blessing of wealth.

• To warn those who denied the Prophet (ﷺ) and opposed him in order to turn him away from prayer and from calling to guidance, and to threaten them with the severest kinds of punishment; and to strengthen the Prophet (ﷺ) and his followers by informing them that God knows the plots of their enemies, that He will subdue them and support the people of truth, so they should not heed their enemies.

[Tafsir]

Recite, O Prophet, what has been revealed to you of the Qur'an, beginning with the name of your Lord, who alone creates, who created every human being from a thick, red clot of blood. Recite, O Prophet, what has been revealed to you; indeed your Lord is abundantly bountiful and vast in generosity, who taught His creation writing by the pen, taught man what he did not know, and brought him from the darkness of ignorance into the light of knowledge.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 96, verses 9–12:

Have you seen how strange is the arrogance of this man, Abu Jahl, who forbids a servant of Ours from praying to his Lord, when that servant is Muhammad (ﷺ)? Have you seen, if the one being forbidden from prayer is upon guidance, how can he forbid him? Or if he (Muhammad) is one who commands others to righteousness, would he (Abu Jahl) forbid him from that?

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 96, verse 13–19:

Have you considered: if this one who forbids (the Prophet) denies what he is called to, and turns away from it, does he not know that Allah sees everything he does? It is not as Abu Jahl claims. If this one does not desist from his opposition and his harm, We will surely seize him by the forelock, a harsh seizing, and he will surely be cast into the Fire. A forelock that is lying in what it says, sinning in what it does. As if lying and error were manifest in it. So let this tyrant summon the people of his assembly, the ones he seeks help from; We will call the angels of punishment. It is not as Abu Jahl supposes. Indeed, he will not harm you, O Messenger, in any way, so do not obey him in what he calls you to, of abandoning the prayer, and prostrate to your Lord, and draw near to Him by devotion, through obeying Him.
